messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED · reserved-gpu-pool-us-west-2-resv-3 crossing 98% utilization for 6m. Alert level: P1. Autoscaler attempted +2 instances, received quota/limit error. Creating thread.
oncall_morgan: on it. page goes to me. what's the customer impact? :eyes:
alex_prod: seeing queue growth on resv-3, avg queue depth 380 -> requests/sec for reserved tenants down 35%, tail latency 2.1s -> 18s on long jobs. KoiHealth (tenant:koihealth) has multiple running jobs in reserved slot and 5 requests 503ing.
priya_sre: confirmed autoscaler error: "QuotaExceeded: GPUs per project limit reached" in cloud logs. Attempts to spin up failed. autoscaler logs attached:```
Error: Requesting GPUs failed
CloudAPI: quotaExceeded: GPUs vCPUs per region limit
at autoscaler.go:412
```
ops-bot: Added tag incident:reserved-pool-pressure, linked runbook: https://intra.ops/runbooks/reserved-pool-pressure
oncall_morgan: priority: protect reserved tenants first (KoiHealth paying reserved contract). Who can evict non-reserved / lower-pri jobs now?
jordan_eng: I can run eviction script for non-reserved pool jobs. prepping command:```
# evict preemptible jobs on pool resv-3
./infra evict --pool resv-3 --filter "priority<50" --dry-run
```
alex_prod: queue shows ~55% of queued tokens from non-reserved burst jobs (batch ingestion). Evicting those should free ~6 GPUs worth. we need ~8 GPUs to stabilize.
priya_sre: note: autoscaler also hitting deploy-api rate limit, we are seeing 429 on createInstance. Might be hitting cloud provider regional rate limits + quota. Working with cloud infra to request soft limit increase but will take 30-90m.
oncall_morgan: run evict now. jordan, coordinate with priya to avoid evicting any reserved-tagged workloads. tara_support, please open CS ticket to KoiHealth and tell them we're mitigating and will update in 15m.
tara_support: on it. drafting message: "We're aware of degraded inference performance for your dedicated pool in us-west-2. Our on-call is actively mitigating; we may route short-term traffic to hosted fallback. ETA 15-30m." send?
oncall_morgan: yes send. alex, capture exact examples for customer.
alex_prod: copying sample logs for KoiHealth:```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] tenant=koihealth request_id=abc123 status=503 reason="no available capacity"
[2026-03-15T10:12:14Z] tenant=koihealth request_id=abc124 latency=18234ms
```
jordan_eng: running eviction (no dry-run). Command:```
./infra evict --pool resv-3 --filter "priority<50" --confirm
```
jordan_eng: eviction started. evicted 42 tasks, freed 5 GPUs (approx). queue depth down to 210.
ops-bot: Automation: throttle low-priority queued jobs on resv-3 enabled (rate=20r/s).
priya_sre: attempted autoscale again -> still failing with quotaExceeded on createInstance. Cloud support opened case case-98765, requested emergency quota bump.
oncall_morgan: intermediate mitigation: enable tenant routing fallback for KoiHealth to hosted-fallback-us-west-2 (not reserved, higher cost but preserves availability). Priya, any objections?
priya_sre: risk: hosted fallback has lower throughput and different latency SLOs, but better than 503s. Approve.
alan_ops: (not on thread) added: we have spare capacity in resv-4 in us-west-2b but it's reserved for another client. Can we borrow temporarily? need sales/legal approval for cross-tenant reassignment.
oncall_morgan: do not reassign reserved capacity without approval. Use hosted fallback first. tara_support: telling KoiHealth about fallback option now. message sent, awaiting ack.
tara_support: customer replied: "Please route anything that preserves throughput, we can tolerate some latency. Keep us posted."
ops-bot: routing change executed: koihealth -> hosted-fallback-us-west-2 (sticky).
alex_prod: traffic for KoiHealth routing began at 10:18Z, error rate down to 8% from 22%, p95 latency ~5.2s. Not ideal but stable.
priya_sre: continuing to push cloud quota request; ETA from provider supportive team ~25-40m. Also ramping up manual scale using standby project in same org (requires infra approval).
oncall_morgan: summarize next steps: 1) monitor queued depth 2) keep eviction + throttling in place 3) notify sales/legal if borrowing needed 4) CS to keep customer notified 5) escalate to infra manager for emergency quota approval.
jordan_eng: queued depth trending down to 120. If we can free 3 more GPUs we'll be back to normal. evicting a few more low-pri jobs now.
ops-bot: Incident note appended: mitigation: eviction + throttling + tenant routing fallback.
priya_sre: autoscaler create calls now returning 200 for first two attempts — provider applied temporary increase. spinning up 3 instances.
jordan_eng: new instances joined, freed capacity +3 GPUs. queue depth 42, tail latency 1.8s.
oncall_morgan: great. revert throttles once stable. tara_support: updating ticket to KoiHealth: mitigated, now monitoring, ETA for full return 30m while autoscaler catches up.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (P1 -> monitoring) · reserved-gpu-pool-us-west-2-resv-3 utilization back to 72% after scale/evict, affected tenants routed/mitigated. Close after 2h of stable telemetry.
priya_sre: follow-ups: - runbook gaps: add step for immediate tenant fallback routing - add play to request emergency cross-tenant borrow approval - add cloud quota pre-req check to autoscaler.
oncall_morgan: assigning follow-ups to eng and infra. good job team. :thumbsup:
